issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The solution repository introduces an additional 'age' attribute on Animal and defines constructors Animal(String name, int age) and corresponding concrete animal constructors with (String, int). The problem statement and the template's Main use/expect single-argument constructors for animals (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")), and the UML/problem text describes Animal as only having a name attribute. This discrepancy can confuse students about the expected constructor signatures and may cause compilation or usage errors with the provided Main or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the 'age' attribute from the solution's Animal and change concrete animal constructors to accept only a single String name parameter (matching the UML/problem and template Main), or (B) update the problem statement and template Main to document and use the additional 'age' attribute and two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Prefer option (A) to align the solution with the UML and the provided template Main.

issues.description: Constructor/API mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the problem statement and the template's Main use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")) and the UML/problem text only describes a name attribute, but the solution's Animal and subclass constructors require an additional int age parameter (e.g., Animal(String name, int age)). This divergence breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description and starter Main to the provided solution API and will confuse students implementing or testing constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor APIs across artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) Modify the solution to match the problem/template by removing the extra age attribute and providing single-argument constructors Animal(String name) and corresponding subclass constructors (e.g., Seal(String name)), or (B) If age is required, update the problem statement and the template Main to document and use constructors with (String name, int age) consistently (or provide overloaded constructors in the solution that accept a single String to preserve compatibility).
